data.title: Cache
data.tagline: Keep reusable results so later requests do not always return to the origin
data.learningOutcome: You can use the scope of stale content to distinguish a browser, shared/CDN, or origin problem and choose a matching check.
data.description: When new CSS is deployed but an old style remains visible, the browser, a shared cache, or a CDN may still be reusing an older copy. Caching reduces waiting and repeated transfer; diagnose the layer that served the old result, because clearing one browser does not prove a shared cache or origin has changed.

learning.assumes: You have seen a hard refresh change a page or different devices show different versions of one URL.
learning.outcome: You can use the scope of stale content to distinguish a browser, shared/CDN, or origin problem and choose a matching check.

explanation.title: A hit reuses a stored copy
explanation.text: When a browser or shared cache finds a reusable response, it can return the resource without contacting the origin, reducing wait and transfer. A request result does not always come from the origin.

explanation.title: An old copy can be revalidated
explanation.text: When a copy is stale, a cache may ask the origin whether it changed. An unchanged resource can produce 304; a changed one returns new content. Diagnose updates with hit, revalidation, and invalidation evidence.

data.boundary: A cache stores reusable response results. Browser Storage keeps a site's user data in the current browser. A CDN is a common shared-cache and delivery layer. Clearing one browser tests only its local cache; it cannot prove that a CDN or origin has updated. DNS caching is also not page-content caching.

lessonPractice.title: Your cleared browser now shows the new CSS, but people elsewhere still see the old version. What should you check first?

options.label: Check shared-cache or CDN hits, response headers, and whether the old copy was invalidated
options.feedback: Correct. A fresh local result but stale results elsewhere points beyond one browser, so verify the shared cache with external requests and response evidence.

options.label: Keep clearing localStorage because every old page comes from browser-saved data
options.feedback: localStorage stores web data, not general HTTP response copies. The local browser is already fresh, and the symptom is wider than one browser.

options.label: Edit the CSS source again without checking which resource version the request received
options.feedback: The source may already be correct. Re-editing hides where the resource came from; check shared caching and response headers first.

data.agentPrompt: Find out whether this old CSS comes from the browser cache, a CDN/shared cache, or the origin. Check the resource URL, response headers, and requests from different locations. Then invalidate the old copy or update the resource address as appropriate, and verify both local and external requests. Do not treat Browser Storage as the cache diagnosis.
